ia-board-chair.summary: Your County Supervisor card names the supervisors, and in 38 of Iowa's 99 counties it now also says which one chairs the board. In the other 61 it cannot: nothing published there pairs a chair with a name.
ia-board-chair.why: No statewide publisher records the chair, so it comes from each county's own board page or its own minutes — and most counties name it on neither, refuse this app outright, or word it too loosely for any reading to be safe to ship.
ia-board-chair.wanted: A county board page or set of minutes that names the chair beside the member, or a statewide list carrying a chair column — the supervisors' own association directory names every member and would need only that one field.

ia-municipal-officeholders.summary: The City card names your city and nothing else — not your mayor, not your council, not your clerk. That is true in 834 of Iowa's 939 cities; in the other 105 either the city or its county publishes them.
ia-municipal-officeholders.why: No one publishes Iowa's city officeholders in one place, and the cities do not publish alike: two in five have no website at all. Nine counties do publish every city inside them, which is where most of the named ones come from.
ia-municipal-officeholders.wanted: More counties publishing their cities' officials the way nine already do, or a city's own council page. Best of all, one statewide list of Iowa's city clerks — the shape Wisconsin's Elections Commission supplies for its municipalities.

ia-polling-places.summary: Your precinct card names your precinct and cannot tell you where to vote in it. The state does publish every polling place in Iowa — but nothing published says which precinct each one serves.
ia-polling-places.why: The two things needed exist in different files. Everything that says which precinct a place serves is two years old; the current list dropped that column, so nothing joins it to a precinct without going through a stale map.
ia-polling-places.wanted: The precinct name carried alongside each polling place in the current file, as the previous edition carried it — one column, and the card could name your polling place. Failing that, any published pairing of precinct to place.

ia-supervisor-count-disagrees.summary: In Warren and Wright Counties your supervisor card names the county and no supervisors. Two state sources disagree about how many seats each board has, so nothing here can say who fills them.
ia-supervisor-count-disagrees.why: The statewide directory lists five supervisors for each county where the state's own district map draws three seats. Nothing published says which is out of date, and naming five people would claim a board this app cannot confirm.
ia-supervisor-count-disagrees.wanted: Either source corrected so the two agree, or each county's own published roster of the supervisors sitting today.

ia-supervisor-count-impossible.area: Adair, Floyd, Humboldt, Lucas, Pottawattamie and Tama Counties, Iowa
ia-supervisor-count-impossible.summary: In six Iowa counties your supervisor card names the county and no supervisors. The directory this app reads gives those boards a size Iowa law does not allow, so nothing here can say who sits on them.
ia-supervisor-count-impossible.why: Iowa law puts a board of supervisors at three members or five. The statewide directory lists four, two or six for these counties, which makes that table stale rather than the board unusual, so the names beside it are not printed.
ia-supervisor-count-impossible.wanted: Each county's own published list of its supervisors, or a corrected statewide directory whose board size matches what the county itself reports.

ia-supervisor-district-seats.area: Black Hawk, Butler, Calhoun, Cass, Chickasaw, Dickinson, Guthrie, Howard, Ida, Kossuth, Lee, Montgomery, Osceola, Palo Alto, Sioux, Washington, Winnebago and Worth Counties, Iowa
ia-supervisor-district-seats.summary: Your County Supervisor card shows the district you live in and names the people on the board, and cannot say which of them holds your district. That is true in 18 Iowa counties, all of which elect their supervisors by district.
ia-supervisor-district-seats.why: The statewide map draws each county's districts and records no supervisor against them; the directory that names the supervisors carries no district beside a name. Both halves are published and nothing joins them.
ia-supervisor-district-seats.wanted: Any list a county publishes that prints a district number beside a supervisor's name — a board page, a certified election summary, or a county directory that carries the district.

johnson-county-supervisor-districts.summary: Johnson County's supervisor card names the county and says its districts are pending — it cannot yet tell you which of the five you live in.
johnson-county-supervisor-districts.why: The county adopted five districts for the November 2026 election but publishes them only as a printed map, and the statewide layer this app reads still carries the county under its older at-large form.
johnson-county-supervisor-districts.wanted: A map of the five districts the county can share as data, or a link to one — the way Black Hawk County publishes its own.

jones-county-supervisor.summary: Jones County carries no supervisor-district card at all — the county is entirely absent from the state's own statewide aggregate.
jones-county-supervisor.why: The Iowa Legislature's own CountySupervisorDistricts layer is this app's only statewide source, and Jones County has zero rows in it — measured both by name and by its own FIPS code (105), not a naming mismatch.
jones-county-supervisor.wanted: The county's own GIS file for the districts its own map already shows, or the state adding Jones to its statewide aggregate. Not an extraction from that published map — it carries no usable shapes, which was measured rather than assumed.

marion-council-roster.summary: Marion elects its council by ward, and its ward boundaries are already measured and ready — but no ward card ships, because nothing here can name the four members who hold those seats.
marion-council-roster.why: The city's own website refuses this app's requests outright, and every other publisher checked maps its wards without naming its council: the county draws the boundaries, and no directory carries the people.
marion-council-roster.wanted: A council page this app can reach, or the four ward members' names with the ward each holds — the boundary is already built, and the names are all that is missing.
